chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying to my father, who complained to him about the heat of the sun while he was in ihram, and he was being harmed by it, and he said: Do you think that I may cover myself with the edge of my garment?
He said: “There is no harm in that so long as it does not touch your head.”

key_terms.بِطَرَفِ ثَوْبِي: with the edge of my garment
key_terms.حَرَّ الشَّمْسِ: the heat of the sun causing discomfort
key_terms.رَأْسَكَ: your head, which must not be touched in this case
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: Can a person in ihram shield himself from the sun with his garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a muhrim experiencing hardship from the sun. It permits seeking shade with the edge of one’s garment, provided that it does not touch the head, indicating a limit within the rulings of ihram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2682 - It is narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

"I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say to my father, who complained to him about the heat of the sun while he was in the state of ihram and was troubled by it.
He asked, 'Do you think it is permissible for me to cover myself with the edge of my garment?'
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in that as long as it does not touch your head.'"
